title: Pointed morphisms of relative abelian spaces are homomorphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $A\to S$ and $B\to S$ be proper smooth commutative group algebraic spaces of finite presentation [def-trf-algebraic-space] whose geometric fibres are abelian varieties, meaning smooth proper geometrically connected group schemes. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; smoothness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. Let $u:A\to B$ be any $S$-morphism such that $u\circ e_A=e_B$, where $e_A,e_B$ are the identity sections. Then $u$ is a homomorphism: $u\circ m_A=m_B\circ(u\times_Su)$, with $m_A,m_B$ the addition maps. This assertion holds over nonreduced bases and after any locally Noetherian base change. In particular, if $C\to S$ is another such space and $v:A\times_SB\to C$ is a morphism whose restrictions to $A\times e_B$ and $e_A\times B$ are both zero, then $v=0$.

source.place: I section 1, rigidity and homomorphisms, for the field argument; relative input Mumford--Fogarty--Kirwan, Geometric Invariant Theory, Proposition 6.1 (WANTED). proof.text: We first prove the stated two-axis vanishing assertion, with arbitrary spaces $P,Q,R$ satisfying the hypotheses on $A,B,C$ and $w:P\times_SQ\to R$ zero on both identity axes. On every etale scheme chart, smoothness implies flatness by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]; the chartwise definition therefore makes $P\to S$ flat. Each geometric fibre of $P$ is geometrically integral by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], applied to its smooth proper connected group scheme. Hence every fibre $P_s$ over $\kappa(s)$ is geometrically integral: for a field extension $K/\kappa(s)$ with algebraic closure $\bar K$, the base change $P_{\bar K}\to P_K$ is surjective and, on etale charts, faithfully flat, so $P_K$ is reduced because $P_{\bar K}$ is, and $|P_K|$ is irreducible as the continuous image of the irreducible $|P_{\bar K}|$; $P_K$ is separated over $K$, hence decent. The identity is a section. Thus the first assertion of [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard] applies: for every scheme $T\to S$, the canonical map $\mathcal O_T\to(p_T)_*\mathcal O_{P_T}$ is an isomorphism. Only this global-functions assertion is used, not any Picard-space construction.

source.place: Tag 0E0S, lemma-proper-flat-geom-red-connected; the existing rigidified-Picard node states the needed universal structure-sheaf conclusion.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$. The fibres $P_{\bar s},Q_{\bar s},R_{\bar s}$ are schemes by hypothesis. Apply [lem-sc-rigidity] to $w_{\bar s}$ with $X=P_{\bar s}$, $Y=Q_{\bar s}$ and $Z=R_{\bar s}$. The source factor is proper, geometrically connected and geometrically reduced by the preceding characterization; the second factor is connected; the target is proper, hence separated and of finite type. The fibre at $e_Q$ maps to the single point $e_R$. Consequently $w_{\bar s}=g\operatorname{pr}_2$. Composing with $(e_P,1)$ gives $g=0$ because the other axis is zero. Hence $w_{\bar s}=0$ as a scheme morphism for every $\bar s$.

source.place: I Theorem 1.1, printed pp.8--9; field rigidity in the existing node gives the scheme-theoretic factorization.

proof.text: Take a surjective etale scheme atlas of $Q$, and restrict it to affine opens $T$. This is allowed by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Pull back $w$ to a $T$-map $h:P_T\to R_T$. The projection $P_T\to T$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], since it is a base change of $P\to S$; similarly $R_T\to T$ is proper, hence separated and locally of finite type. At every geometric point of $T$, step 2 says $h$ is the constant identity map, so its image is a singleton. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-space-finite-image-neighbourhood] at each $t\in T$. It supplies affine open neighbourhoods $V$ covering $T$ and actual factorizations $P_V\xrightarrow{a}Z\xrightarrow{j}R_V$, with $Z$ an affine scheme finite over $V$.

source.place: Tag 0AEJ, lemma-flat-proper-family-cannot-collapse-fibre, applied over each atlas scheme T.

proof.text: For each such $V$, put $p_V:P_V\to V$ and $s_V=(e_P)_V:V\to P_V$. Step 1 identifies $p_V^\sharp:\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\to\Gamma(P_V,\mathcal O)$ as an isomorphism. Since $p_Vs_V=1$, we have $s_V^\sharp=(p_V^\sharp)^{-1}$. Let $b=as_V:V\to Z$. Then $(bp_V)^\sharp=p_V^\sharp s_V^\sharp a^\sharp=a^\sharp$. By the injectivity in [lem-sfb-space-affine-target-global-functions], $a=bp_V$. Thus $h|_{P_V}=jbp_V$. The axis hypothesis says $jb=hs_V=e_R|_V$, so $h|_{P_V}=0$. The calculation takes place in the full rings of global functions, including their nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 05Z1, lemma-morphism-to-affine-scheme; combine with the universal functions conclusion already obtained in step 1.

proof.text: It follows that the pullback of $w$ to every atlas open $T$ is zero. To descend this equality, take any scheme test $U\to P\times_SQ$. The $Q$-coordinate lifts etale locally on $U$ to the chosen atlas; on these lifts $w$ and zero agree. The target $R$ is a sheaf, so its two sections over $U$ agree. This holds for every test $U$, hence $w=0$ as a natural transformation. This proves the two-axis assertion without reducing the base.

source.place: Definition of algebraic spaces as fppf sheaves with an etale atlas; etale-local uniqueness of sections.

proof.text: Apply the assertion just proved to $P=Q=A$, $R=B$, and the morphism $d(x,y)=u(x+y)-u(x)-u(y)$, defined using the given group operations. Because $u(e_A)=e_B$, both restrictions $d(x,0)$ and $d(0,y)$ are zero. Thus $d=0$, which is precisely $u\circ m_A=m_B\circ(u\times_Su)$. Applying the same assertion to $P=A,Q=B,R=C,w=v$ proves the last clause. Finally the equality for $u$ pulls back along any base change: both sides are composites of the pulled-back maps and group operations. In particular it holds after every locally Noetherian base change, including nonreduced ones.
